text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on Mixtral-8B when serving the latest AWQ-int8 build after the RoPE scaling tweak. p95 latency for gen-only routes jumped ~38% and memory climbs faster on long-chat sessions.

maya: ugh. Is this only on AWQ-int8 or do GPTQ/FP8 variants show it too?

sam: quick summary of what I saw from the profiler on one replica:
```
# profiler snippet (served with kernel-selector=auto)
model: mixtral-8b-awq-int8
seq: 1024 (chat), batch: 4
kernels chosen: matmul_generic, rotary_rope_fallback
cpu->gpu memcpy spikes at step 12
KV cache growth: ~1.8x expected by step 40
p95 latency: 210ms -> 290ms
```

ingrid: curious about the "rotary_rope_fallback" — that suggests the optimized RoPE kernel wasn't selected. Could be because RoPE scaling changed the qk layout and kernel selector no longer matches the signature.

alex: agreed. after the RoPE scale param change (PR #4122) some signature fields moved from float32->float16 during compilation. Selector logic matches dtype+shape -> it may fall back to generic.

maya: @sam can you dump the kernel selection trace for a failing request? there should be a selector log in /var/log/redwood/runtime/kernel_select.log with lines like: `pick_kernel(model, op_id=...)`.

sam: here you go (trimmed):
```
pick_kernel: op=rotary_rope, shape=(4,8,64,64), dtype=float16 -> try optimized_rope_v2 (requires scale<=1.0) -> mismatch scale=1.2 -> fallback matmul_generic
pick_kernel: op=attn_matmul, shape=(4,8,64,64), dtype=int8 -> chose matmul_generic
```

alex: scale=1.2 is the new change. optimized_rope_v2 assumed canonical scale <=1.0 to reuse precomputed cos/sin tables. If scale>1 we recompute and the kernel marked incompatible.

taylor: two avenues: 1) expand optimized_rope_v2 predicate to accept scaled tables or 2) add a separate rope_scaled kernel that handles scale>1 fast. Short-term we could force kernel preference by env var `RW_KERNEL_PREFER=optimized_rope_v2` for a canary.

ingrid: also the AWQ int8 path seems to change dtype combos. AWQ packer emits int8 kernels + per-head scales that the kernel selector currently treats as unusual shape -> falling back. We need to update selector rules for AWQ packing pattern.

maya: before we tweak selector, can we run an experiment: revert RoPE scale param for canary traffic and compare? That isolates whether AWQ packing or the scale caused the regression.

alex: good idea. I'm going to roll a canary config that pins RoPE scale back to 1.0 for Mixtral AWQ endpoints and run 5k requests of our calibration prompts.

perf-bot: deploy started: canary mixtral-8b-awq-int8 @ canary-3 (rollout id c-6672).

sam: preliminary results after 2k reqs: p95 back down to 220ms (was 290ms), KV growth within expected bounds. So scale change looks like main trigger for kernel fallback.

taylor: still need to ensure accuracy isn't affected if we revert. Did we capture eval deltas vs calibration set?

alex: yes — had evaluation on 60-shot calibration prompts. AWQ-int8 with scale=1.2 had -0.6 BLEU relative to baseline fp16 on a small set; scale=1.0 returns to within -0.12. So both perf and quality prefer scale=1.0 in current runtime.

ingrid: notes for follow-ups:
- update kernel selector rules to recognize AWQ int8 pack patterns (per-head scale arrays) so we don't fallback to matmul_generic
- add `rotary_scale` predicate in optimized_rope_v2 kernel so scale !=1.0 can still use optimized path when precompute is feasible
- add unit test for selector with mixtral/mistral dimension combos & int8 packer metadata
- measure memory/KV effects when scale !=1.0 (we saw 1.8x KV growth)

maya: I'll open a ticket consolidating these action items and assign to eng-runtime + eng-ml kernel team. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RI-9051 (created).

sam: for immediate mitigation: revert RoPE scale change in PR #4122 and add a follow-up PR that updates kernels + selector. I'll queue revert and notify infra to hold canary until merge.

alex: thanks. Also let's run a quick comparison vs GPTQ: if GPTQ-int8 doesn't trigger the fallback then AWQ packer needs special casing. sam, can you run GPTQ build on the same canary machines?

sam: scheduled. I'll post a short perf matrix when done.

perf-bot: deploy success: revert rolled to canary-3, traffic at 10% currently.

taylor: one more detail — batching heuristic mis-estimation also amplified latency: selector falling back to matmul_generic increased per-token cost which made the dynamic batcher prefer smaller batches (so throughput dropped). We'll include a synthetic that asserts kernel selection impact on batcher decisions.

alex: good catch. If the kernel produces slower op, the batcher should be aware via feedback metric and adjust batch windows. I'll add an experiment to tweak the batcher weight on kernel latency.

ingrid: tagging kernel authors @maya @taylor. Please coordinate on selector patch and new kernel.

maya: ack. I'll pair with sam tomorrow to get traces and a failing unit test.

alex: thanks all — keeping this thread until we close the ticket. :thumbsup:
